finding.claim: The /logo handler passes an unauthenticated user-supplied URL to http.Get after only a substring check for 'example.io', so an attacker can reach internal or metadata endpoints and read the response.

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") — attacker-controlled query or body parameter
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") — substring check only; not a host allowlist
http.Get(raw) — default client follows redirects; request dispatched to attacker-chosen host
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) — response body returned to attacker (full-read SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at line 32 does not close the finding: the host is never parsed or compared, a fragment such as '#example.io' satisfies it without being sent to the server, and redirects are followed by default so an allowlisted host can redirect to 169.254.169.254 or RFC-1918 addresses. No scheme restriction is present, but Go's http client only supports http and https. Endpoint is unauthenticated and listens on all interfaces (:8081).

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring test at main.go:32 (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which does not close the finding. No host parsing, allowlist, or redirect restriction exists between main.go:31 and main.go:36. The /cdn handler's noRedirect and trusted-host map at main.go:10-12, 20, and 24 are not on the /logo path.
verdict.reason: At main.go:31 the value comes straight from r.FormValue("logo") with no authentication, and at main.go:32 a substring match on "example.io" passes an attacker URL such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io to the default http.Get at main.go:36, whose body is copied back to the client at main.go:38.
